sentences.text: Above writ petition is filed challenging Ext.P5 revised valuation statement issued by the 3 rd respondent and for a further direction to respondents 4 and 5 not to purchase the property of the 6th respondent by executing sale deed without obtaining the sanction of the District Collector and obtain a suitability certificate from the Deputy Director of Panchayat.
3. It is averred that the petitioner is the owner in possession of 4.5 acres of land in Sy.No.124/1 and 124/2 of Anickadu Village, Kottayam District.
The 5th respondent Panchayat decided to purchase land for purpose of construction of a public crematorium.
It is contended that the 4th respondent who is in good releationship with the 6th respondent informed the 6th respondent about the project.
The 6th respondent who was in dire need of money approached the 4th respondent Secretary with an offer to give 18.90 ares of land for 2025:KER:1267 double the rate at Rs.70,000/- per cent.
The 4 th respondent Secretary immediately at her own instance decided to purchase the entire 18.90 ares of land without even studying the suitability of the land for the proposed project.
The 4th respondent by Ext.P1 requested to the 3rd respondent to issue a valuation certificate for the said property.
In furtherance of Ext.P1 the 3rd respondent sought a report from the Village Officer and Ext.P2 valuation report was submitted by the Village Officer.
4. It is contended that a perusal of Ext.P2 would reveal that the fair value of the property is only Rs.30,000/- per Are.
But as per Ext.P3 valuation report the price of the land was fixed at Rs.73,389/- per Are.

The 4th respondent aggrieved by the valuation in Ext.P3 approached the 2nd respondent to reconsider the same as per Ext.P4 letter which is alleged to have been done at her own instance without even getting the approval of the committee.
It is contended that all these has been done by the 4 th respondent only to help the 6th respondent.

The 2nd respondent by Ext.P5 order directed to reconsider Ext.P3 certificate and in furtherance of the same, Ext.P5 revised certificate was issued, wherein the valuation of the property was shown as RS.1,47,781/- per Are.
It is the case of the petitioner that in a short span of four months the value was increased by more than 100%.
Petitioner would contend that the requirement of the 2025:KER:1267 Panchayat is only 10.12 Ares but the 6th respondent was not prepared to sell her property in part.
Thereupon the Panchayat is now proposing a new project for construction of a Material Recovery Facility/Centre and to acquire entire extent of property of the 6 th respondent for these two projects.

Aggreived by the same,
Ext.P6 complaint was preferred before the 1st respondent.
But the 1st respondent has not considered the same till date.
It is aggrieved by the revised valuation now fixed as per Ext.P5 that the present writ petition has been filed.
5. A detailed counter affidavit has been filed by the 4 th respondent.

Originially the Panchayat has sanctioned the project in the year 2021-22 for constructing a public crematorium, the need of which was felt by the Panchayat during the outbreak of Covid-19 pandemic, where the Panchayat had to make request to other Panchayats for the burial of persons who died due to Covid-19.
A Central Financial Commission grant of Rs.15,50,000/- was also obtained for the said purpose.
Thereupon as per Ext.R4(a) resolution the Panchayat committee decided to purchase land for construction of a public crematorium.
Proposals were invited from land owners who are willing to transfer their land to the Panchayat as per Ext.R4(b) and R4(c) paper publication.
Only two persons i.e. respondent Nos.6 and one Aravinda Charitable Society expressed 2025:KER:1267 their willingness to transfer their land for establishment of public crematorium.

sentences.text: The property of the 6th respondent was found to be situated in close proximity to the burrial ground of Mar Gregorius Orthodox Church, Pallickathodu.
The experience of the Panchayat is that whenever they tried to locate a place for establishing crematorium general public raised objection regarding the same.

Only minimum objection from the public was found as regards establishment of a gas crematorium in the property of the 6 th respondent, primarily due to the existence of another burial ground in its close proximity.

It is true that only 25 cents were required for construction of the public crematorium, but respondent No.6 was not ready to fragment her property and the price originally approved by the 3rd respondent Tahsildar was also not accepted by the 6 th respondent.
In such circumstance the Panchayat could not purchase the property during 2021-22 and the fund available was carried on to 2022-23 as spill over fund.
During 2022-23 Central Finance Commission issued further grant of Rs.12,52,980/- for the purpose of sanitation.
The Panchayat has found that the disposal of non- biodegradable waste predominantly plastic waste caused a serious 2025:KER:1267 problem at the Panchayat.
Thereupon in 2018 a shed was constructed for this purpose in the open playground owned by the Panchayat and the same was found to be not workable due to the close proximity of an Anganwadi.

As a stop gap arrangement two rooms of Panchayat shopping complex has been set apart from the said buiding, and the the same was also found not feasible at it was very close to the building constructed by the Panchayat for rehabilitation of mentally challenged persons.
Thereupon a decision was taken to purchase property for establishing the Material Collection Centre, and again public notification was issued.
While so, Ext.P5 revised valuation certificate was issued by the 3 rd respondent Panchayat for the property of the 6 th respondent.
Thereupon the 6 th respondent again submitted a proposal with respect to her property having an extent of 18.9 ares.

As it was found that the property could be purchased to locate both the projects, Panchayat decided to purchase the property of the 6 th respondent for the project for establishing MCF collection unit also as per Ext.R4(e) decision.

It is further submitted that as per Rule 5(1) of the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Burial and Burning Grounds)
Rules, 1998 for construction of gas crematorium, only 25 metres distance is necessary from the nearby residential house, and going by Ext.R4(f) the site is in a non- objectionable point.

Further there is no objection from any authority that the land currently used for MCF is not suitable, and as under this project, only plastic waste are collected from homes and segregated, and the present property is more than sufficient for the said project.
Contention that the site is beyond 25 metres from residential houses is without any basis.
Further sanction from the District Collector has not been obtained for construction of a crematorium.

sentences.text: It was further contended that the 2nd respondent has directed the 3rd 2025:KER:1267 respondent to reconsider Ext.P3 valuation certificate after considering Document No.730 of 2022 of Vazhoor SRO, but the same was not done while issuing Ext.P5 revised valuation report.

It is further submitted that on 31.03.2022 meeting of the Panchayat committee was held without proper notice on the committee members and a decision was taken to buy the property of the 6 th respondent by paying 30% more than the valuation amount.

It is the 4th respondent on her own volition approached the Revenue Divisional Officer for enhancement of fair value and the same was done suppressing the same to the Panchayat Committee.
7.

An additional counter affidavit was filed by respondents 4 and 5, wherein it is stated that the present collection centre is conducted in a shopping complex and since the Buds School for differently abled children is situated in close proximity to the same, Ombudsman for Local Self-Government Institutions by order dated 10.07.2023 directed shifting of the waste collection centre from the shopping complex of the Panchayat, and presently it is continuing on the strength of an interim order passed by this Court in WP(C) No.35264/2023.

Later on, the Panchayat considered the main objection of the petitioner regarding suitability of the property for construction of a burial ground and decided to give up the project for establishment of a public crematorium, but at the same time the 2025:KER:1267 Panchayat committee found it necessarily to establish MCFC with more facilities for the collection and processing of the waste disposal.

Accordingly Ext.R4(i) decision was taken by the Panchayat committee not to pursue the establishment of a public crematorium in view of the legal objection and to utilise the said space and fund set apart for the said project for establishing the MCFC.
Later on, the Panchayat as per Ext.R4(j) decision decided to expand the project of waste disposal.
This was at a time when the Panchayat is being accused for not carrying out waste disposal work.
It is further submitted that as per Ext.R4(m) the District DPC has also approved the new project for the enhanced amount.

8. A statement has been filed by the 3 rd respondent as directed by this Court on 19.07.2024,
wherein it is stated that Ext.P5 revised valuation certificate was issued after verifying 10 sale deeds of similar area and considered the average sale price of five sale deeds most equivalent to the property involved and refix the land value as Rs.1,47,781/- per Are.
As per Report No.278/22 after site inspection, Charge Officer also reported that Rs.1,47,781/- per Are is to be considered as the land value of the property.

On the basis of the same, it is argued that the contention of the petitioner that Ext.P5 revised valuation certificate was issued without considering any document eventhough a specific direction was issued by the 2025:KER:1267 Revenue Divisional Officer to look into similar documents.

It is further submitted by the learned Standing Counsel for the Panchayat that Exts.R4(g) and R4(h) were issued after conducting site inspection and the same was duly referred to in Exts.R4(g) and R4(h).
9.

The above writ petition is filed seeking to quash Exts.P4 and P5 suitability certificates issued by the Deputy Director of Panchayat and also seeking to quash Ext.P3, the decision of the Sub- Collector, Kottayam wherein direction was issued to the Tahsildar to refix the valuation of the property pursuant to which Ext.P5 valuation certificate was issued.
10. I have considered the rival contentions on both sides.

sentences.text: Going by the averment in WP(C) No.25810 of 2022, the case of the petitioner is that for construction of a public crematorium, Panchayat committee sanctioned an amount of Rs.15,05,000/- for purchase of 10.12 ares for the proposed project, and the 4th respondent Secretary who was in good relationship with the 6th respondent informed about this project to the 6 th respondent, and immediately the 6th respondent who was in dire need of money and who was struggling to sell her property approached the 4 th respondent and gave an offer at the rate of Rs.70,000/- per cent, 2025
: KER:1267 and the 4th respondent Secretary immediately at her own instance desired to purchase the entire 18.90 ares of land without studying the suitability of the land for the proposed project.
But the contention raised in the said writ petition is quite contrary to the facts discernible from the counter affidavit filed by the 4 th respondent.
As per Ext.R4(a) a decision was taken by the Panchayat committee for construction of a public crematorium.
Thereafter proposals from land owners who are willing to transfer the land to the Panchayat was made through paper publication evidenced by Exts.R4(b) and R4(c).

Two persons submitted their willingness including the 6th respondent, and the other proposal was rejected as there was huge liability upon the said property and the property of the 6th respondent was accepted especially taking into consideration the fact that the said property is very near to the burial ground of Mar Gregorius Orthodox Church.
As evident from Ext.R4(f) sketch it is contended that the present property of the 6 th respondent is one in which minimum objection was raised by the public for establishment of a gas crematorium.
It is further submitted that though valuation certificate was issued earlier, as per Ext.P2 the same was not acceptable to the 6th respondent and the Panchayat also felt that the value fixed is low.
Thereupon an appeal was preferred before the RDO.
While so, further funds were received by the Panchayat for 2025:KER:1267 sanitation purposes.
Thereupon the Panchayat committee decided to purchase the property for establishment of a material collection centre, to which also public notification was issued.
It is at this point of time an appeal was preferred against the valuation certificate issued by the 3rd respondent Tahsildar.
Thereupon Ext.R4(e) decision was taken to purchase the land of the 6 th respondent which is to be utilised for both crematorium as well as material collection centre.
While so, the appeal was allowed and remitted back to the Tahsildar for reconsideration, and Ext.P5 revised valuation statement was issued.

It is to be noted that the facts discernible from the counter affidavit would reveal that the averment in the writ petition especially in paragraph 2 and 3, is not in accordance with the facts of the case.

The averment that no decision was taken by the Panchayat committee to purchase the property and that the decision of the Panchayat was intimated by the 4 th respondent to the 6th respondent who are in good releationship are all without any basis especially in the light of Ext.R4(a) decision of the Panchayat committee, and Exts.R4(b) and R4(c) paper publications and Ext.R4(e) decision of the Panchayat committee to include the establishment of material collection centre in the very same property.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that steps for 2025:KER:1267 purchase of the property was done without following the procedures and is done in a surreptitious manner cannot be accepted.
12. Further aspect to be considered is that the objection regarding starting of a public crematorium is no longer existing since the Panchayat committee itself have decided to drop the said project.

As per Ext.R4(i) decision the committee of the Panchayath decided not to proceed with the establishment of public crematorium in view of the objections and decided to utilise the space and fund for setting apart an MCFC unit.

In view of the above facts and circumstances it is seen that the grievance raised by the petitioner regarding establishment of a public crematorium no longer exists.
What remains is only the construction of a material collection centre in the property proposed to be purchased from the 6th respondent.
Petitioner himself in the reply affidavit has admitted that what is being done in the MCF Centre is collection of plastic waste alone.
Therefore, the petitioner can have absolutely no objection on the ground of any environmental issues due to the starting of the MCFC project.

The contention raised by the petitioner objecting to the establishment of 2025:KER:1267 a material collection facility centre in the property of the 6 th respondent is that there is no necessity for shifting the material collection facility centre from the present location to the property of the 6th respondent.

The counter affidavit filed by the respondent Panchayat would reveal that it was initially conducted in a shed constructed in an open playground and the same was found not workable as it is situated in close proximity to the anganwadi.
Thereupon as a stop gap arrangement two rooms of Panchayat shopping complex was set apart from the said project.
But the said two shop rooms in the Panchayat shopping complex were in close proximity to the Buds School started for differently abled children.

Thereupon a complaint was preferred before the Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions and as per order dated 10.07.2023 the Ombudsman directed to shift the waste collection centre from the shopping complex of the Panchayat, and that the present unit is functioning in the said shopping complex only on the strength of an interim order passed by this Court in WP(C) No.35264 of 2023 filed by the 4th respondent Panchayat.

It is contended that since the 6th respondent insisted that the property will not be sold in fragments the Panchayat committee had to decide to purchase the whole of the land and decided that in the said land both material collection facility centre as well as public crematorium could be 2025:KER:1267 established.

Now the proposal for public crematorium is already dropped and the Panchayat committee decided to establish the material collection facility centre in the said property so that it could be shifted from the shopping complex which is very near to the Bud School for differently abled children, as per the direction of the Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions.
It is also to be seen that as per Ext.R4(j) decision of the Panchayat committee the committee has decided to expand the project of waste disposal.
The learned Counsel for the 6th respondent brought to my notice Section 178 of the Panchayati Raj Act which enables the Panchayat to acquire immovable property.

Rule 178 is extracted below for reference:-
"178. Acquisition of immovable property required by the panchayat.

- Any immovable property which is required by a panchayat for a public purpose connected with the discharge of the functions imposed on it under this Act, or the rules or bye-laws made there under, or any other law, may be acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Central Act 1 of 1894) and on payment of compensation awarded under that Act in respect of such property and of any other charges incurred in acquiring it, the said property shall stand transferred to and vest in the Panchayat:
Provided that nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to prevent any panchayat from acquiring immovable property either through private purchase or any free surrender."

sentences.text: Going by Section 178 the Panchayat could either seek for acquisition of land through the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act or acquire immovable property either through private purchases over any free surrender.
The Rule relevant for consideration is the Kerala Panchayati Raj (Acquisition and Disposal of Property) Rules, 2005.

sentences.text:
Rule 3 deals with power to acquire property which is extracted below:-
"3. Power to acquire property.--(1) A Panchayat may acquire any land or building within or outside its area either by purchase or otherwise-in order to introduce any public facility or for providing any service, and may with the prior approval of the Government dispose of any of its property either by sale or otherwise.

( 2) The acquisition of land under sub-rule (1) may either be in accordance with the Land Acquisition Act for the time being in force and the rules made thereunder or through private purchase or free surrender.

(3) A Panchayat, before acquiring any land under sub-rule (1) shall comply with the following conditions, namely:--
(a) Suitability certificate to the effect that the proposed land is suitable for the p r o p o s e d p u r p o s e s h a l l b e o b t a i n e d f r o m t h e D e p u t y D i r e c t o r o f Panchayats/Assistant Development Commissioner/District Collector in the case of Village/Block/District Panchayats respectively.

(b) If the proposed property is for educational purpose, permission from the. Deputy Director of Education shall be obtained.
2025:KER:1267 (c) Permission from the District Medical Officer shall be obtained in the case of Hospitals,
Dispensaries etc."

Going by Rule 3(a), before acquiring the property suitability certificate to the effect that the proposed land is suitable for the proposed purpose shall be obtained from the Deputy Director of Panchayat.
It is submitted that the same has been obtained by the Panchayat as evident from Exts.R4(g) and R4(h).
The only contention raised by the petitioner is that the same has been issued without conducting a site inspection.
But a perusal of Exts.R4(g) and R4(h) itself will reveal that the same has been issued after verifying the documents and after conducting a site inspection.

The learned Counsel apearing for the 6th respondent also brought to my notice Section 20A of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 which mandates that, for infrastructure projects the Court should not grant any injunction stopping the construction of the projects which are scheduled in the Act.

"Sanitation"
is one project which come under the schedule of the Act, which is the project now envisaged by the Panchayat.

14. Taking into consideration the above facts and circumstances and the contentions of both sides,
and taking into consideration the fact that the Material Collection Centre is only for collecting plastic materials, where it is segregated even going by the averment in the reply affidavit of the V.X. sentences.text: petitioner, I am of the view that 2025:KER:1267 no interference is called for in these writ petitions.

The Panchayat has gone for the enhancement in the valuation due to the objection on the part of the 6th respondent that they are not ready to sell the property for the said value and on finding that the value fixed by the Tahsildar was low when compared to neighbouring properties, and also taking into consideration the statement filed by the 3 rd respondent that valuation has been fixed after verifying the sale deeds of similar area and considering the average sale price of five sale deeds most equivalent to the property involved and refixation was done after considering all this.

Though the learned Counsel for the petitioner would submit that there are allegations against the particular Village Officer who is involved in the valuation of the property, it is to be seen that it is not just the Village Officer who has verified the said sale deeds but Charge Officer has also conducted a site inspection and reported that Rs.1,47,781/- per Are is to be considered as the land value of the property.
All procedures for purchasing the land was followed by the respondent Panchayat.
Out of the two proposals submitted only the proposal of the 6 th respondent was found to be non-objectionable but the 6 th respondent insisted that the whole of the property should be purchased.
It is common knowledge that there will be serious obstruction from the nearby residents to any proposal for starting a 2025:KER:1267 crematorium or a waste collection centre.
The property of the 6 th respondent was found to be less objectionable as it was nearby an existing burial ground of the church.
Panchayat as an Institution for Local Self Government is duly bound to provide for crematorium and material collection centres for the benefit of the people residing therein.
Therefore the decision of the Panchayat to purchase the property of the 6th respondent for starting the material collection centre, for which there is less objection cannot be found fault with.
Taking into consideration the above facts and circumstances, none of the contentions raised by the petitioner is sustainable, and accordingly both the writ petitions are dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The 5th respondent Panchayat decided to purchase land for purpose of construction of a public crematorium.
Thereupon as per Ext.R4(a) resolution the Panchayat committee decided to purchase land for construction of a public crematorium.
Only minimum objection from the public was found as regards establishment of a gas crematorium in the property of the 6 th respondent, primarily due to the existence of another burial ground in its close proximity.
In such circumstance the Panchayat could not purchase the property during 2021-22 and the fund available was carried on to 2022-23 as spill over fund.
Ext.R4(g) and R4(h) were issued without conducting a site inspection, and without proper V.X. Antony vs The District Collector on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14939870/
5 application of mind.
Thereupon an appeal was preferred before the RDO.
Thereupon the Panchayat committee decided to purchase the property for establishment of a material collection centre, to which also public notification was issued.
While so, the appeal was allowed and remitted back to the Tahsildar for reconsideration, and Ext.P5 revised valuation statement was issued.
The averment that no decision was taken by the Panchayat committee to purchase the property and that the decision of the Panchayat was intimated by the 4 th respondent to the 6th respondent who are in good releationship are all without any basis especially in the light of Ext.R4(a) decision of the Panchayat committee, and Exts.R4(b) and R4(c) paper publications and Ext.R4(e) decision of the Panchayat committee to include the establishment of material collection centre in the very same property.
As per Ext.R4(i) decision the committee of the Panchayath decided not to proceed with the establishment of public crematorium in view of the objections and decided to utilise the space and fund for setting apart an MCFC unit.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The counter affidavit filed by the respondent Panchayat would reveal that it was initially conducted in a shed constructed in an open playground and the same was found not workable as it is situated in close proximity to the anganwadi.
Thereupon as a stop gap arrangement two rooms of Panchayat shopping complex was set apart from the said project.
Thereupon a complaint was preferred before the Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions and as per order dated 10.07.2023 the Ombudsman directed to shift the waste collection centre from the shopping complex of the Panchayat, and that the present unit is functioning in the said shopping complex only on the strength of an interim order passed by this Court in WP(C) No.35264 of 2023 filed by the 4th respondent Panchayat.
The learned Counsel for the 6th respondent brought to my notice Section 178 of the Panchayati Raj Act which enables the Panchayat to acquire immovable property.
The learned Counsel apearing for the 6th respondent also brought to my notice Section 20A of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 which mandates that, for infrastructure projects the Court should not grant any injunction stopping the construction of the projects which are scheduled in the Act.

But a perusal of Exts.R4(g) and R4(h) itself will reveal that the same has been issued after verifying the documents and after conducting a site inspection.

is one project which come under the schedule of the Act, which is the project now envisaged by the Panchayat.

The Panchayat has gone for the enhancement in the valuation due to the objection on the part of the 6th respondent that they are not ready to sell the property for the said value and on finding that the value fixed by the Tahsildar was low when compared to neighbouring properties, and also taking into consideration the statement filed by the 3 rd respondent that valuation has been fixed after verifying the sale deeds of similar area and considering the average sale price of five sale deeds most equivalent to the property involved and refixation was done after considering all this.
opennyai_summary.decision:
All procedures for purchasing the land was followed by the respondent Panchayat.
Out of the two proposals submitted only the proposal of the 6 th respondent was found to be non-objectionable but the 6 th respondent insisted that the whole of the property should be purchased.
The property of the 6 th respondent was found to be less objectionable as it was nearby an existing burial ground of the church.
Panchayat as an Institution for Local Self Government is duly bound to provide for crematorium and material collection centres for the benefit of the people residing therein.
Therefore the decision of the Panchayat to purchase the property of the 6th respondent for starting the material collection centre, for which there is less objection cannot be found fault with.
Taking into consideration the above facts and circumstances, none of the contentions raised by the petitioner is sustainable, and accordingly both the writ petitions are dismissed.
